name: Hong Seok-joh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2024); Hurun Global (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Hong Seok-joh heads BGF Retail, one of Korea's largest convenience store companies.
Operating under the brand name CU, BGF boasts more than 18,000 stores.
His sister, Hong Ra-hee, is the widow of the late Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee.
Prior to his start in the business, Hong was a prosecutor.
forbes_facts: The business got its start in 1989 via a franchise-licensing agreement between the Hong family's Bokwang Group and Japanese convenience store operator FamilyMart.
His late father was the chairman of JoongAng Ilbo, one of South Korea's largest newspapers.

name: Jonas Kamprad
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Jonas and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Jonas, the middle child, studied industrial and furniture design in Switzerland and applied his skills in Ikea-run subsidiary Habitat.
He is a board member of Netherlands-based Ikea parent Stichting INGKA Foundation and Ikano Group.
forbes_facts: Ingvar Kamprad ranked among the top 10 richest people for years before lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control.

name: Albert Nahmad
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Albert Nahmad is CEO and approximately 7% shareholder of Watsco, a large distributor of air conditioning, heating and refrigeration parts.
Born in Panama, Nahmad emigrated to the United States to study engineering at the University of New Mexico and Purdue.
In 1973, Nahmad bought a stake in Watsco, then a small, publicly traded company.
Using a highly acquisitive strategy, Nahmad helped Watsco grow from a market cap of $22 million in 1989 to more than $20 billion now.
Nahmad's children are active in his businesses. His son is president of Watsco; his daughter is president of the Nahmad Family Foundation.

name: Ajit Gupta
forbes_bio: Ajit Gupta is Chairman of Park Medi World, which debuted on the Indian bourses in December 2025.
Park Medi has 17 hospitals and nearly 4,300 beds and is the second largest hospital chain in North India.It is looking to add five more hospitals by fiscal 2028.
In 2005 he set up the Park Hospital in New Delhi, which eventually became part of Park Medi World.
The hospitals offer a range of specialties from cardiology and neurology to oncology and  gastroenterology.
Son Ankit Gupta is the managing director.
forbes_facts: He started his career as a junior resident at Safdarjung Hospital

name: Sandy Weill
forbes_bio: Sanford "Sandy" Weill spent decades in financial services, culminating with Travelers and Citicorp merging to form Citigroup in 1998.
Weill's first job was a Bear Stearns runner in 1955, earning $150 a week.
He formed a brokerage firm with partners, built it into Shearson Loeb Rhoads, and sold it to American Express for nearly $1 billion in 1981.
Weill was CEO of Citigroup until 2003 and chairman until 2006.
He is still an active investor, president of the board of trustees at Carnegie Hall and on the executive council at UC San Francisco.
forbes_facts: When Weill first got married, he and his wife lived with her parents.
Weill's protege at Travelers and Citigroup was Jamie Dimon, who left in 2000 to be CEO of Bank One (now JP Morgan Chase).

name: Dennis Anthony Uy
forbes_bio: Dennis Uy and his wife Maria founded Converge ICT Solutions, one of the Philippines' largest operators of high-speed internet.
They took the company public in 2020, raising more than $500 million in what was one of the Philippines' largest IPOs in recent years.
Maria serves as the company's president, Dennis as its CEO. The couple remains majority owners of the company.
Converge ICT's fixed broadband services now reach more than 9.6 million homes in 440 cities and municipalities in the Philippines.
forbes_facts: Dennis used to work as a maintenance boy, tinkering refrigerators at his uncle's business.
With a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, he is the only CEO of a major Philippine internet company who has a tech background.

name: Alexander Vik
forbes_bio: Alexander Vik comes from a wealthy family of fur merchants and has dabbled in everything from closed-end country funds to insurance and tech startups.
He remains locked in a contentious legal battle with Deutsche Bank, which in late 2013 obtained a $250 million judgment against his trading operation.
Deutsche had sued the trading operation, based largely out of Vik's Connecticut home, over a margin call that went unpaid during the financial crisis.
So far Vik is not paying and has appealed the London court's judgment.
Meanwhile Deutsche has started legal proceedings in New York, Connecticut, Delaware and Oslo to investigate Vik's assets.
forbes_facts: A Norwegian who was raised in Sweden and schooled in the Canary Islands, Vik was a former golf champion at Harvard University.
During the first Internet bubble, Vik was behind Xcelera.com, one of the biggest dot.com boom and bust stocks of the era.

name: Lee Sang-ryul
forbes_bio: Lee Sang-ryul is founder and co-CEO of Chunbo, a chemicals company, which he started in 1997.
Lee's wife, Seo Ja-won, is the other co-CEO of Chunbo.
The company specializes in making chemicals for lithium-ion batteries that power electric vehicles.
Lee was formerly head of development at Hanvit Chemical, a cleaning-supplies maker.

name: Chalerm Harnphanich
forbes_bio: Physician Chalerm Harnphanich owns a substantial stake in listed Bangkok Chain Hospital.
Chalerm runs the company together with his wife Somporn, daughters Pornluck and Pornsuda and son Kantaporn.
Bangkok Chain has 14 hospitals in all with 2,144 beds.
Chalerm is preparing to open a new hospital in Vietnam.
forbes_facts: He got his start in 1984 with the 60-bed Kasemrad hospital in Bangkok.
